income_group_note: High and low Table 7 GMM coefficients and signs of three-way interactions match; middle-income groups genuinely not covered (Limitations p.7093).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: only internal lagged instruments, no instrument count, Sargan 543.16 vs Hansen 34.86 in HICs and AR(2) -4.21 contradict validity, while causal wording is used.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: moderate is reasonable since fixed telephone and secure servers per million (HIC max 277,133.7) are weak proxies and mobile is absent.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: moderate fits since only the extreme low and high income groups are used, middle-income excluded for data reasons, and obs counts differ (1160 vs 1102).
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: GDP per capita is a standard output measure, but data were normalised before estimation and units/transform of the dependent variable are unclear.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: serious is justified by one-proxy-at-a-time models, trade openness divided by GDP per capita, sign flips across models, and stars that do not match brackets; critical could be argued.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: moderate is fair because all models are shown but the text conclusions contradict the tables in several places.
risk_of_bias.why: Dynamic GMM with unverified instruments and internal table inconsistencies leaves exogeneity unestablished and causal claims ('impact', 'proved') overreach; serious fits, with critical a defensible alternative.
